facts.statement: Listrognathosuchus was an extinct genus of alligatoroid crocodilian.
facts.quote: Listrognathosuchus is an extinct genus of alligatoroid crocodilian.

facts.statement: The generic name Listrognathosuchus was established in 1997 to replace Leidyosuchus for the species L. multidentatus.
facts.quote: In 1997, the generic name replaced that of Leidyosuchus for the species L. multidentatus

facts.statement: The species was first described by Charles Mook in 1930.
facts.quote: "L." multidentalis was first described by Charles Mook in 1930

facts.statement: The fossils were found in Torrejon Arroyo, New Mexico.
facts.quote: found from a locality in Torrejon Arroyo, New Mexico

facts.statement: Fossils of Listrognathosuchus date back to the middle Paleocene epoch.
facts.quote: Fossils date back to the middle Paleocene epoch.

facts.statement: The animal lived from 63.4 to 60.9 million years ago during the Danian to Selandian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Selandian (63.4 to 60.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Listrognathosuchus is closely related to Borealosuchus.
facts.quote: Listrognathosuchus is closely related to Borealosuchus

facts.statement: Researchers have debated whether it belonged to Diplocynodontinae, was a relative of later crocodylids, or formed its own subfamily called Leidysuchinae.
facts.quote: It was suggested to be a possible member of Diplocynodontinae or a relative of later crocodylids, and even as a member of its own subfamily of broad snouted early eusuchians, Leidysuchinae.

facts.statement: It is classified in the family Alligatoridae.

rejected.statement: The holotype consists of a partial vertebral column, mandible, partial left ilium, and left tibia.
rejected.quote: consisting of a partial vertebral column, mandible, partial left ilium, and left tibia
